text: The SOC Operations course taught correlation rules as vendor-neutral pseudocode: a source, a grouping key, a threshold inside a time window, then an alert. That logic has to live somewhere real in an actual SIEM. In Microsoft Sentinel, it lives in an Analytics rule, and the general-purpose type you write yourself is called a Scheduled Analytics Rule.

A scheduled rule is built from a real KQL query plus scheduling settings, created under Microsoft Sentinel, Configuration, Analytics, Create, Scheduled query rule. Every time the schedule fires, Sentinel re-runs that query and checks the result count against a threshold. That's the same source, grouping, threshold, and action shape from the prior course, now expressed as a concrete, running rule instead of pseudocode.

Four settings define it: the query itself, written on the rule's Set rule logic tab; Run query every (how often it executes, as often as every 5 minutes, up to every 14 days); Lookup data from the last (how far back each run scans); and the alert threshold, which is the result count that has to be crossed, usually greater than zero. When a run's results cross that threshold, Sentinel generates an alert, which event grouping and alert grouping settings then route into a new or existing incident.

Run frequency and lookback aren't independent settings. Log ingestion into the workspace takes time, so an event that happens just before a run but hasn't finished ingesting yet can fall into the gap between two runs and never get evaluated by either one. Microsoft's own guidance is to set the lookback window longer than the run frequency, commonly double, specifically to absorb that ingestion delay rather than leaving a silent, hard-to-notice blind spot in coverage.

That's the engine behind every scheduled rule: a query, a schedule, a threshold, and a lookback window set wide enough to avoid gaps. Next, Lesson 10 looks at where that query actually comes from — writing one from scratch, or starting from one of the hundreds of built-in rule templates Microsoft already ships.
